title: Why forbid what Allah made lawful for you?
subtitle: A gentle correction over a cup of honey
then: Aishah narrated that the Prophet ﷺ drank honey at Zaynab bint Jahsh's house, and some of his wives agreed to tell him he smelled of maghafir, a strong gum. He said he would never drink it again. {idea}Allah asked why he would forbid what Allah had made lawful{/idea}, to please his wives, and ended: {reward}Allah is Forgiving, Merciful{/reward}.
now: Your in-laws frown at something perfectly halal, so you quietly give it up for good. A friend teases you about a harmless habit, and you swear you will stop. {idea}Only Allah draws the lines.{/idea} Giving up what He allowed, just to keep the peace, is not piety.
old: Giving up something halal to please people is a kind of goodness.
new: Only Allah decides what is lawful, and I do not have to forbid His gifts to please anyone.
try: Notice one halal thing you have been avoiding only because of someone's opinion, and let yourself enjoy it with thanks.

title: Allah has given you a way out of your oaths.
subtitle: A rash promise does not have to become a prison
then: The Prophet ﷺ had sworn he would not drink the honey again. Allah told the believers that {reward}He had already given them a way to release themselves from their oaths{/reward}. And {idea}Allah is your Protector, the All-Knowing, the All-Wise{/idea}.
now: In a heated moment you swore you would never speak to your cousin again, never go back to that masjid, never forgive. {reward}Allah made a way out of oaths like that.{/reward} {idea}Ask someone with knowledge how, and walk back through the door.{/idea}
old: I swore it, so now I am stuck with it.
new: Allah gave a way out of rash oaths, because He is my Protector, not my jailer.
try: If you are holding on to an angry vow, ask a trusted scholar this week how to release yourself from it.

title: Who told you? The All-Knowing, the All-Aware.
subtitle: A secret shared, and a gentle way of raising it
then: Hisham said the secret was the Prophet's ﷺ words: I will not drink it again, I have sworn, so tell no one. It was shared anyway, and Allah told him. {reward}He mentioned part of it and let part go.{/reward} When she asked who told him, he said: {idea}the All-Knowing, the All-Aware{/idea}.
now: You find out your sister told the family something you said in confidence. You could list every word. {reward}Raise it, but do not drag every detail into the light.{/reward} {idea}And remember: nothing you share in secret is hidden from Allah either.{/idea}
old: When someone betrays my trust, I should lay out every detail.
new: I can address a wrong while still letting part of it go, and Allah already knows it all.
try: Keep one secret someone told you today, fully, even when it would be fun to share.

title: If you both turn back to Allah, your hearts are inclined.
subtitle: The door of repentance, even in a family quarrel
then: Umar told Ibn Abbas the two wives addressed here were Aishah and Hafsah. Allah first opens the door: {reward}if you turn to Allah in repentance, your hearts are already inclined to it{/reward}. Then He makes clear that {idea}Allah, Jibril, the righteous believers and the angels stand with His Prophet ﷺ{/idea}.
now: You and a sibling quietly ganged up on a parent, or you and a coworker made someone look bad. {trap}It is tempting to keep the story going.{/trap} {reward}The verse offers the first exit: turn back, your heart already wants to.{/reward}
old: Once I have taken a side in a quarrel, I have to stick with it.
new: I can turn back to Allah at any point, and my heart is often ready before my pride.
try: If you have been part of a small plot against someone, end it today with one kind word to them.

title: What makes a spouse truly good.
subtitle: A list of qualities, not looks or status
then: The passage closes with a serious reminder to the Prophet's ﷺ wives: his Lord could give him others better. Then it names what "better" means: {reward}submitting, believing, devout, repenting, worshipping, fasting{/reward}. {idea}Every quality on the list is about the heart and worship.{/idea}
now: The rishta conversation. Job, height, family name, which city. {idea}This verse has its own list, and none of it is on a CV.{/idea} {reward}It is also a list to become, not just to look for.{/reward}
old: A good spouse is someone impressive on paper.
new: A truly good spouse is one who submits, believes, repents and worships, and I can work on being one.
try: Pick one quality from this list and do one act of it today, for the people you live with.

title: Protect yourselves and your families from the Fire.
subtitle: Faith is something you carry home
then: Ibn Abbas explained: {idea}work in Allah's obedience, avoid disobedience, and tell your family to remember Allah{/idea}, and Allah will save you from the Fire. Qatadah said a person helps his family act on Allah's commands. The verse describes angels over the Fire who {trap}never disobey what Allah commands{/trap}.
now: Dinner with the phones out, Fajr nobody gets up for, the kids learning everything from YouTube. {idea}You cannot hand this to the weekend school.{/idea} {reward}Start with yourself, then gently bring them along: a dua at dinner, praying together once a day.{/reward}
old: My family's faith is their own business, or the teachers' job.
new: I am asked to guard myself and help my family, starting with my own example.
try: Pray one prayer together as a family today, or invite one family member to pray with you.

title: Make no excuses that Day.
subtitle: When excuses stop working
then: Ibn Kathir says on the Day of Resurrection, those who disbelieved will be told: {trap}do not offer any excuse this Day, it will not be accepted{/trap}. They are only repaid for what they used to do. The very next verse calls believers to sincere repentance.
now: You have an excuse ready for everything: the traffic, the kids, the stress, the job. {trap}Excuses work on people.{/trap} {idea}On that Day only deeds will count.{/idea} {reward}Today you can still swap an excuse for a fix.{/reward}
old: I always have a good reason for what I did not do.
new: Excuses end one day, so I want to turn them into changes while I can.
try: Catch yourself making one excuse today, and do the thing instead, even partly.

title: Turn to Allah with sincere repentance.
subtitle: Lord, complete our light and forgive us
then: Ibn Kathir says sincere repentance is {idea}a true, firm turning that erases past sins and moves a person to quit the wrong they used to do{/idea}. When Allah says "perhaps", it means He will. The Prophet ﷺ was heard praying: {reward}O Allah, do not disgrace me on the Day of Resurrection{/reward}.
now: You have said "never again" so many times it feels silly. {reward}The door does not close because you came back again.{/reward} {idea}Make this one firmer: delete the app, change the route home, tell a friend.{/idea}
old: I have repented so many times it does not count anymore.
new: Allah calls me back again, and sincere repentance means making this turn firm.
try: Make one practical change today that makes it harder to return to a sin you have repented from.

title: Strive against denial and hypocrisy, and be firm.
subtitle: No softness toward what is false
then: After the call to repentance, Allah commands His Messenger ﷺ to {idea}strive against the disbelievers and the hypocrites and be firm with them{/idea}. Ibn Kathir says this was an order to the Messenger ﷺ himself, with firmness in this life. {trap}Their refuge is Hell, and wretched is that destination.{/trap}
now: Before you look outward, look in. The prayer you rush when no one is watching. The halal you preach and the haram you hide. {idea}Be firm with that part of yourself.{/idea} {reward}It is the striving that is always open to you.{/reward}
old: Hypocrisy is something other people have.
new: The first hypocrisy I am asked to be firm with is my own.
try: Name one small way you act differently in private than in public, and close that gap today.

title: Married to prophets, and it did not save them.
subtitle: The wives of Nuh and Lut
then: Ibn Kathir says they lived with two prophets, eating and sleeping beside them, {trap}but betrayed them in faith, not in chastity{/trap}. Ibn Abbas said Nuh's wife told his people whenever someone believed, and Lut's wife told the city whenever he had guests. {trap}Their closeness did not help them before Allah.{/trap}
now: Your father is the imam. Your wife is a hafidha. Your best friend is the most religious person you know. {idea}None of that is your faith.{/idea} {reward}It can inspire you, but only your own heart crosses over.{/reward}
old: Being close to religious people makes me safe.
new: Closeness to the righteous helps, but only my own faith will count for me.
try: Do one act of worship today purely on your own, not because someone around you is doing it.

title: My Lord, build me a house near You.
subtitle: Asiyah, wife of the worst tyrant, chose Allah
then: Qatadah said Pharaoh was the most tyrannical man on earth, yet {reward}his wife was not affected by his disbelief, because she obeyed her Lord{/reward}. Her name was Asiyah bint Muzahim. She was punished for believing in the Lord of Musa and Harun, and asked Allah for a house near Him. The Prophet ﷺ named her among the best women of Paradise.
now: Your workplace mocks prayer. Your home is not religious. Your friends think you are strange. {idea}Asiyah lived in Pharaoh's palace.{/idea} {reward}Your environment is real, but it does not get the final say over your heart.{/reward}
old: I cannot be a good Muslim in this environment.
new: Asiyah held on in Pharaoh's house, so my heart can choose Allah wherever I am.
try: Say Asiyah's dua today: Rabbi ibni li 'indaka baytan fil jannah.

title: Maryam, who guarded herself and believed her Lord's words.
subtitle: The surah ends with two women held up as examples
then: Ibn Kathir says Maryam {reward}protected her honor and was free of immorality{/reward}. Allah sent Jibril to her, and so Isa was conceived. She believed in her Lord's words and books and was among the devout. The Prophet ﷺ named her with Khadijah, Fatimah and Asiyah as {reward}the best women of Paradise{/reward}.
now: This surah began with a household quarrel and ends with Asiyah and Maryam as examples for every believer, man or woman. {idea}Purity, belief, and quiet devotion.{/idea} {reward}These are the qualities Allah chose to close it with.{/reward}
old: The great examples of faith are mostly men.
new: Allah set two women as the example for all believers, and their qualities are open to me.
try: Read the story of Maryam in Surah Maryam this week, slowly, and note one quality you want.
